diagrams.caption_semantics: Proposed partition of sensing, low-level control, communications, operator supervision and optional high-level computation. Every actuator request terminates at the low-level controller; sensing feedback and autonomous computation require implementation and verification.
limitations: Reported devices do not establish validated interfaces, feedback or autonomy.
Actuator feedback denotes proposed angle, speed, joint/current measurements.
Hardware interruption is represented within the actuation/protection block; its circuit is specified separately.
The page shows selected functional interfaces, not an exhaustive network topology or wiring schematic.
routing_notes: Use a two-row three-column grid in the specified positions.
Draw each opposing data/control or control/feedback pair as two offset directed lines, not one ambiguous bidirectional arrow.
Route Mega-to-companion diagonal connections through separate left-side/row-gap lanes.
Operator commands return through communications and Mega; do not draw a dashboard-to-actuator bypass.

diagrams.caption_semantics: Proposed protected distribution with four parallel load branches. Branch regulation, conductor ratings and protective-device selection require identified hardware and measured loads.
limitations: Motor, sensor, logic and steering/arm branches are parallel loads, not a series chain.
Supply returns and connector pinouts are omitted from this functional diagram.
A proposed companion computer requires its own correctly rated supply within the logic branch.
Motor energy interruption does not imply that removing arm power is safe; holding/parking is addressed by the protective-state design.
routing_notes: Place a common protected-distribution spine in the gap between rows and connect each lower branch to it.
Use filled junction dots only where branches join that supply spine.
Draw no motor-to-arm, arm-to-logic or logic-to-sensor power arrow.
The single legend entry is electrical power supply.

diagrams.caption_semantics: Proposed allocation of a permitted body-motion request to four steering and wheel-speed channels. Measured-state returns close the channel loops and inform feasibility and command restrictions.
limitations: Feedback hardware and closed-loop tracking have not been verified on the photographed rover.
The kinematic relation assumes locally planar, rigid-body rolling.
Equivalent reversed wheel rotation is allowed only within identified steering and cable limits.
No unrestricted steering, point-turn capability or measured path accuracy is claimed.
routing_notes: Keep the top-row command path left-to-right and continue from kinematics down to limits and left to actuator channels.
Feedback is a measurement source; its directed return arrows must terminate at channels, limits and arbiter.
Route the feedback-to-limits connection below the lower row so it does not pass through the actuator block.
Use distinct control and feedback line styles.

diagrams.caption_semantics: Proposed wheel-speed feedback and supervisory traction monitoring. Encoder speed returns to the PI loop; independent motion and electrical checks can request derating or stopping.
limitations: The diagram represents proposed control and sensing, not validated installed feedback.
A tracking residual alone is not a direct slip measurement.
Independent body velocity must not be inferred solely from the same wheel encoders used in the comparison.
Protective response here is supervisory control; the independently defined emergency energy-interruption circuit is separate.
routing_notes: Place a visible checks-to-PI feedback return up the middle column.
Route the protective-response-to-PI command through an outer left lane.
Mechanical torque/motion from drive to contact uses physical-transfer styling, not electrical-supply styling.
Do not leave the PI block as an open chain without its encoder-speed return.

diagrams.caption_semantics: Proposed gas-measurement architecture linking identified MQ variants, heater-aware acquisition, environmental covariates and reference-based calibration. Outputs retain calibration and validity status.
limitations: An exact MQ variant must be identified before selecting heater voltage and timing.
MQ channels are not assumed chemically selective or calibrated on the rover.
Environmental context is an independent calibration input, not the output of the ADC stage.
Invalid or out-of-domain conditions require status flags; no supported concentration is inferred from an uncalibrated response.
routing_notes: Use separate opposing lines between MQ channels and conditioning: measurement data forward, heater power backward.
Acquisition and environmental context independently feed calibration.
Route acquisition-to-calibration through the inter-row gap; do not imply that acquisition creates temperature or humidity measurements.
The data legend includes analog measurements and their associated digital records.

diagrams.caption_semantics: Proposed particulate-measurement chain combining representative airflow, device-level checks and independently acquired environmental covariates. Correction and mapping require reference validation, time alignment and pose information.
limitations: PMS7003 channel names are reported outputs, not proof of calibrated mass concentration.
Humidity sensing and mapping are proposed additions.
Reference co-location and temporal validation are required before assigning a correction.
Raw measurements and quality flags remain available beside adjusted values.
routing_notes: The inlet-to-sensor arrow is a physical airflow path; all later arrows carry data.
Validation and environmental context converge independently on calibration.
Draw no serial-validation-to-context arrow.
Use separate inter-row lanes for validation-to-calibration and context-to-calibration so every arrowhead is visible.

diagrams.caption_semantics: Parallel ultraviolet and pressure/temperature measurement paths converge at quality checks and logging. UV conversion depends on board identification and optical calibration; the BMP180 has no humidity channel.
limitations: UV conditioning and BMP180 are separate measurement paths.
GUVA identity alone does not establish irradiance or ultraviolet-index calibration.
BMP180 temperature can be affected by board heating.
Pressure-derived altitude depends on atmospheric conditions and is not an independent terrain-height measurement.
routing_notes: Keep GUVA-to-UV-conditioning across the top-left pair and BMP180-to-pressure-processing across the bottom-left pair.
Merge both paths at quality checks, then connect quality checks to logging.
Route pressure-processing-to-quality-checks through the inter-row gap.
Do not connect UV conditioning to BMP180 as if one drives the other.
